clue.text: In spite of that, always superior?

explanation.surface: Someone insists that whatever happens, they are always on top.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as three words: never the lesser one, so always the superior.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means notwithstanding or all the same; split into words it says something is at no time inferior.

clue.text: Scene of Blondin's famous crossing

parts.note: Charles Blondin, the French acrobat, crossed the gorge below the great falls on the US-Canada border on a tightrope in 1859

explanation.definitionFit: The waterfall on the US-Canada border is where the tightrope walker made his celebrated walk across a high wire.

clue.text: It is Eve who gets a caller

definitions.text: It is Eve who gets a caller

parts.words: It is Eve who gets a caller
parts.note: the person who receives a visitor is described, and the words 'It is Eve' hold exactly the letters needed, rearranged

explanation.surface: Eve is the one with someone knocking at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: An old-style clue with no anagram signal: the seven letters of IT IS EVE rearrange to the answer, and the rest describes the person called upon.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who receives a visit is the counterpart of the visitor, just as an employee is of an employer.

clue.text: Poet, even if "Anon." is not Mr. Blank

definitions.text: Poet, even if "Anon." is not Mr. Blank

parts.words: Poet, even if "Anon." is not Mr. Blank
parts.note: a versifier who stays anonymous but does not write blank verse, so must make lines chime at their ends

explanation.surface: An unnamed poet is still somebody, not a mere Mr Blank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mr. Blank' looks like a nameless man, matching 'Anon.', but it means a writer of blank verse, which has no rhymes.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of light or jingling verse is a poet whose lines chime at the ends, unlike blank verse.

clue.text: Erica among the athletes

indicators.note: the letters sit among the words that follow, spanning the join of 'the' and 'athletes'

explanation.surface: A woman named Erica is running with the athletes.
explanation.walkthrough: Erica looks like a woman's name, but it is the botanical genus of heathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is the Latin genus name for heather plants.

clue.text: Purple medick found in Switzerland

explanation.surface: A purple flower grows in the Swiss Alps.
explanation.definitionFit: Purple medick is the fodder plant also called alfalfa; the same name belongs to a Swiss city and its lake.

clue.text: Colourful display of carpets

parts.note: bands of colour laid out as light is split, with the word 'carpets' holding exactly the letters needed, rearranged

explanation.surface: Rugs laid out in a riot of colour.
explanation.walkthrough: An old-style clue with no anagram signal: the letters of CARPETS rearrange to the answer, the bands of colour shown when light is split by a prism.
explanation.definitionFit: When light is dispersed by a prism it shows bands of colour, each such band-set being one of the plural forms.

clue.text: Last drop of beer ?

parts.note: bitter is a British style of beer, so its final drop could be called its final part; the phrase also means the very last point

explanation.surface: Draining a glass of beer down to the dregs.
explanation.walkthrough: Bitter is a British ale; the phrase meaning 'to the very last' reads literally as the tail of the pint.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means the very last point, however painful, while a bitter is a type of beer.

clue.text: Report two sides of conversation

parts.note: one side of a conversation is listening, to hear
the other side of a conversation is speaking, to say

explanation.surface: An account of a chat between two people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two sides' looks like first and last letters of 'conversation', but it means listening and speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: Hearsay is rumour or second-hand report, information passed on that one did not witness.

clue.text: Their aim is to strike gold

definitions.text: Their aim is to strike gold

parts.words: Their aim is to strike gold
parts.note: the gold is the bullseye at the centre of a target, so these people aim to hit it, not to find treasure

explanation.definitionFit: In target shooting with bows the central ring is coloured gold, and hitting it is the best score.

clue.text: They are not necessarily mendacious

parts.note: a tale-teller can mean a liar, but one who tells stories may simply be a narrator

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old euphemism for liars, but narrators of fiction need not be dishonest.

clue.text: Good Lord, deliver us from one of the long-leggety variety

definitions.text: Good Lord, deliver us from one of the long-leggety variety

parts.words: Good Lord, deliver us from one of the long-leggety variety
parts.note: quotes the old Scottish prayer asking deliverance from ghoulies, ghosties and long-legged creatures that go bump in the night

explanation.surface: A prayer for protection from some spindly creature.
explanation.walkthrough: The Cornish or Scottish litany runs 'From ghoulies and ghosties and long-leggety beasties ... Good Lord, deliver us!'
explanation.definitionFit: A Scots word for a small creature or animal, the one named in the traditional prayer.

clue.text: Character in Hamlet and Hair too, perhaps

indicators.note: signals the letters of 'Hair too' may be rearranged into another word

explanation.surface: Hamlet and the musical Hair both have a role worth naming.
explanation.walkthrough: Hair looks like the title of the musical, set beside Hamlet, but with 'too' it is the letters to shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Hamlet's loyal friend, who survives to tell his story, is a character in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: This craft may have following winds

definitions.text: This craft may have following winds

parts.words: This craft may have following winds
parts.note: craft as a skilled occupation, not a boat; the steady tropical winds named after commerce follow its name

explanation.definitionFit: A trade is a skilled craft or occupation, and the steady easterly tropical winds bear the same name.

clue.text: One kind of truck a railway takes to the end of a long journey

definitions.text: the end of a long journey

parts.note: a tipper is a lorry that tips its load out

explanation.surface: A goods wagon carried by rail all the way to its destination.
explanation.walkthrough: The song says 'It's a long way to Tipperary', the Irish town, so it is where a long journey ends.
explanation.definitionFit: The First World War marching song makes the Irish town the goal of a long way travelled.

clue.text: This asylum is mainly for foreigners

definitions.text: This asylum is mainly for foreigners

parts.words: This asylum is mainly for foreigners
parts.note: asylum here is refuge granted by a state to people fleeing persecution abroad, not a hospital

explanation.definitionFit: Refuge granted to those persecuted for their beliefs abroad is the protection most often sought by people from other countries.

clue.text: A mere help, maybe, just for a day

indicators.note: suggests the letters of 'A mere help' could come out in another order

explanation.surface: A little help that lasts only a single day.
explanation.definitionFit: Something short-lived, from the Greek for lasting a day, like a mayfly.

clue.text: Its men are famed in song

definitions.text: Its men are famed in song

parts.words: Its men are famed in song
parts.note: the Welsh song 'Men of ...' celebrates the defenders of a castle town in north Wales

explanation.definitionFit: The castle town in Gwynedd, Wales, is celebrated in the stirring march 'Men of' its name.

clue.text: A note to an American is of the least significance

parts.note: a minim is a musical note, the half note
Al is a common American man's name, as in Al Capone

explanation.surface: A short message sent to someone in the States that matters little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' looks like a letter, but it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tiny or negligible is the smallest possible in amount or importance.

clue.text: An exclusive class of players, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the word for the players is spoken, giving a different spelling

parts.note: the cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A select group of actors, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'class of players' looks like a sporting or acting grade, but 'players' alone is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: A hereditary social rank, closed to outsiders, is a closed class in society.

clue.text: Fanny Burney's fleet-footed heroine?

parts.note: the title character of Burney's 1796 novel shares her name with Virgil's swift warrior maiden in the Aeneid

explanation.definitionFit: Burney's novel has a heroine of this name, which belongs also to the Volscian runner in Virgil, said to skim over corn.

clue.text: When a diner's upset, it could be the fish

indicators.note: upset as in overturned, telling us the letters of 'a diner's' are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken letter for letter, including the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A restaurant customer is upset about what was served.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' looks like the diner's mood, but it signals the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A small oily fish of the herring family, often sold in tins.

clue.text: Antony thought Lepidus meet to be sent on them

definitions.text: Antony thought Lepidus meet to be sent on them

parts.words: Antony thought Lepidus meet to be sent on them
parts.note: in Julius Caesar, Antony calls Lepidus a slight unmeritable man, fit to run small tasks for others

explanation.definitionFit: Short trips to deliver messages or fetch things, which Shakespeare's Antony thinks the junior triumvir fit only for.

clue.text: Ship's crew devoid of craft

indicators.note: devoid of means lacking, so the word for craft is taken out of the phrase

parts.note: a craft is a vessel, a ship

explanation.surface: A vessel's sailors have lost their boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing SHIP from SHIP'S CREW leaves the answer; the whole clue also suggests the propeller, the part of a vessel that is not itself a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's propeller is called its screw, a working part of the vessel rather than a craft itself.

clue.text: Wherein travellers were liable to lose their heads

definitions.text: Wherein travellers were liable to lose their heads

parts.words: Wherein travellers were liable to lose their heads
parts.note: the passengers are prisoners carried to the guillotine in the French Revolution, so losing heads is literal

explanation.definitionFit: The open cart that took the condemned through Paris to execution during the Terror.

clue.text: Joseph, the visionary

explanation.surface: Joseph is described as a man of vision.
explanation.definitionFit: In Genesis Joseph is mocked by his brothers as 'this dreamer'; a visionary is one with fanciful ideas.

clue.text: Painter of sheep-dogs ?

parts.note: the Victorian artist John ..., read as one who deals in collies, the Scottish herding dogs

explanation.definitionFit: John Collier was a Victorian portrait painter, and his surname looks like a word for one who works with collies.

clue.text: The interests of those in the minority?

definitions.text: The interests of those in the minority?

parts.words: The interests of those in the minority?
parts.note: minority here means being under age, not a smaller group, so these interests are those of young people

explanation.definitionFit: Care for the wellbeing of the young, those still legally minors, is a field of social services.
